answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs, and a random sample of its outputs is checked against independently verified results. A mismatch burns part of the stake; repeated failures bar the identity from future work. The stake is a costly signal because creating many identities requires locking real capital in each, while trying to forge reliable outputs risks forfeiting it. A violet badge alone proves nothing; the economic penalty makes Sybil identities expensive to sustain.
